summary: MaterialDNA source-depth finding: maintenance.repairCount is the only canonical recipe integer count currently validated by an unbounded validateNonNegativeInteger(), while recipeVersion and all continuous physical/material fields use explicit bounded domains. The validator therefore accepts arbitrarily large finite integral doubles, including values at/above the exact-integer precision boundary where a conceptual +1 repair cannot be represented as a distinct number. No existing PR/lane found in the live search addresses repairCount; merged #283 covers recipeVersion drift and hostile unknown-key execution instead. Recommend a narrow one-shot MaterialDNA backfill that gives repairCount an explicit bounded canonical domain and pins max/over-max regressions without changing fixture recipe seals unless authored content actually changes.
evidence: src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateMaintenance() delegates maintenance.repairCount to validateNonNegativeInteger(), whose only checks are finite, >=0, and math.floor(value)==value; it has no upper bound.

The same module caps recipeVersion at 2147483647, historyEvents at 32, anomalyModifiers at 8, key length at 160, and assigns explicit maxima to physical dimensions/density/repeats, so repairCount is a domain-boundedness outlier.
tests/materialdna_contract.luau exercises recipeVersion zero/oversized bounds and general recipe validity, but the inspected suite has no repairCount maximum/over-maximum regression.
Repository PR search for repairCount/repair count found only merged MaterialDNA hardening #283, whose documented scope does not include this count domain.

recommendedLane.title: Bound MaterialDNA maintenance repair-count domain
acceptance: choose and document an explicit finite integer maximum for maintenance.repairCount consistent with canonical plain-data/persistence precision needs
maximum value validates and the first out-of-domain value fails closed
existing production fixture references/content seals remain unchanged unless a real authored fixture requires migration
no schema/version bump is assumed without checking whether the tightened domain invalidates any published canonical content
